A regular lattice frame

Source: R/frame.R
areal_lattice.Rd

A frame of nrow x ncol square cells, for examples, simulation studies and testing. Units are numbered row by row from the top left. Square polygons are attached if sf is installed, so the frame can be mapped and survey coordinates assigned to it.

Usage

areal_lattice(nrow, ncol, queen = TRUE, blocks = NULL, cellsize = 10000)

Arguments

nrow, ncol

Number of rows and columns.

queen

Cells sharing only a corner are neighbours (TRUE) or not (FALSE).

blocks

Optional c(rows, cols): adds a grouping block of rectangular blocks of this size (e.g. c(2, 5); one number gives square blocks), for aggregation.

cellsize

Side of a cell in metres; the polygons are placed in a Lambert azimuthal equal-area projection centred on (0, 0) longitude and latitude.

Value

A stareal_frame (see areal_frame()). Ids are "r<i>c<j>".

Examples

fr <- areal_lattice(4, 5, blocks = c(2, 5))
fr
#> <stareal_frame> 20 units, 55 edges (mean 5.5 neighbours), 1 connected component
#>   built from: 4 x 5 lattice
#>   groupings: block (2)
